title: Single-card BF16 decode across three Blackwell SKUs: bandwidth decides c1, power wall caps high concurrency

hardware.gpus: A: RTX 5090 96GB (modded, 575 W); B: RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition 96GB (600 W); C: RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell 72GB (300 W)
hardware.interconnect: irrelevant — TP1, one GPU per machine; A/B are 8-GPU hosts, C is 8x PRO 5000 dual-NUMA PCIe
hardware.topology_summary: single-GPU test on GPU0 of each host
hardware.cpu_numa: A/B: server platforms; C: 2x Xeon 8488C, GPU0 on NUMA0

software.framework_version: 0.32.0 (image vllm/vllm-openai:v0.32.0@befccf0e, same digest on all machines)

model.name: Qwen3.8-27B (official Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B, BF16, 51.75 GiB, hybrid linear-attention architecture)
model.revision: official release, config sha256 verified identical across machines

workload.server_notes: max-model-len 33792, gpu-mem-util 0.85, max-num-batched-tokens 8192; prefix caching ON main pass / OFF control pass; cache-on 3 runs per label + cache-off 1 run. A/B: max-num-seqs 256; C: 128 (72GB card Mamba-cache limit, does not bind below c64). ctx32k_c4 not run on C: 4x32K exceeds its 6.78 GiB KV budget.

results.config: B — RTX PRO 6000 Server 96GB (600 W, ~1597 GB/s)

variance.note: cache-on means of 3 independent runs per label; CV < 0.5% on C (21.94/21.94/21.94 for c1, 300.67/300.81/300.68 for c32); A/B same protocol, 28 runs on B all rc=0. C measured 2026-10-26 after a same-SKU card swap (c1 21.89 pre-swap vs 21.94 post-swap).

methodology: vllm bench serve inside the serving container (server and client same host), random dataset, warmups 10 (c*) / 2 (ctx32k), 3 cache-on repeats per label + 1 cache-off pass with --no-enable-prefix-caching
transferable: Single-stream decode (c1) ranks by memory bandwidth: A (1792) > B (1597) > C — measured 29.68 / 26.10 / 21.94 tok/s

Higher concurrency shifts the bottleneck to compute + power: B's BF16 compute advantage (~1.85x A) shows up progressively (c8 +2.5% -> c32 +13% -> c64 +25%), while C's 300 W power wall makes c32 and c64 IDENTICAL (~300.5 tok/s, +/-0.2%) — a hard throughput ceiling independent of concurrency
Long context (32K prefill) amplifies compute advantage: B beats A by 44% at ctx32k_c4
ShareGPT real-distribution results do NOT extrapolate from fixed-length c64 (B only +3.6% over A there vs +24.7% at c64)
Energy efficiency at c64: B ~1.69 tok/s/W > A ~1.04 > C ~1.02
not_transferable: Multi-GPU conclusions: this study is TP1 by design; see qwen38-27b-8x-72gb-pcie-parallelism.json for C-machine 8-GPU results
ctx32k_c4 on C is physically infeasible (KV budget), so C's long-context concurrency behavior is unmeasured
